subject: Benchmarking MAP: scope, SLOs, and timeline for Acme Retail POC

Subject: Kickoff: MAP + benchmarking plan for POC

Hi Alex / Priya —

Thanks again for taking the call today. Per our discussion, we want to capture a short Mutual Action Plan (MAP) that includes a concrete performance benchmarking plan so your engineering team can validate latency and throughput assumptions before commit. I attached a draft MAP and a starter workload spec to iterate on.

High level ask: can you confirm the primary production workload we should emulate and the acceptance window you'd consider sufficient to advance to procurement? A few things we want to lock down up front so the benchmark is useful:
- Workload profile (typical request size, median/95th token counts, percent of streaming vs non-streaming requests)
- Concurrency target (how many simultaneous sessions)
- Target SLOs you care about (p50/p95 latency, TTFT, throughput)
- Success criteria for the POC (pass/fail gates)
- Timeline: two benchmark runs + decision date

Proposed timeline (draft):
1) Week 0: Finalize MAP & workload spec
2) Week 1–2: Run baseline benchmark (internal) and share results
3) Week 3: Tune/iterate model variant / batching / cache settings
4) Week 4: Final run + executive review + procurement decision

Attachments: acme_map_v1.pdf (MAP draft), benchmark_workload_spec.xlsx (starter).

Looking to schedule a 30-min kickoff to finalize the workload spec tomorrow or Friday. Diego will lead the technical details.

Cheers,

Subject: Re: Kickoff: MAP + benchmarking plan for POC

Thanks Neha — adding a technical proposal for the benchmark so we can converge quickly. I kept it pragmatic so we can run an apples-to-apples test using either a production trace or a synthetic profile derived from it.

Benchmarking plan (technical):
1) Workload definition (we'll want either a 24–72h production trace or these synthetic parameters):
   - Request mix: 70% single-turn completion, 20% multi-turn (avg 3 turns), 10% embedding/rerank
   - Tokens per request: median 64, p95 420
   - Typical prompt + system tokens included in counts
   - Streaming: 40% of requests stream first token immediately
2) Metrics to capture:
   - p50 / p95 / p99 latency (ms) measured for end-to-end request completion
   - Time-to-first-token (TTFT) in ms (critical for perceived latency)
   - Throughput: requests/sec and tokens/sec sustained over 5–15m windows
   - Concurrency: error rate and latency degradation while ramping from 1 -> target concurrency
   - Cost proxy: tokens processed / GPU-hour (for rough economics)
3) Hardware & model variants:
   - Primary: model-x-large (FP16) on A100-40GB (w/ kv cache)
   - Cost-optimized variant: quantized model-x-q4 on T4-like instance
   - Measure both baseline and optimized to show tradeoffs
4) Test procedure:
   - Baseline run: cold-start baseline, single instance, no caching enabled (captures cold path TTFT)
   - Sustained run: ramp to target concurrency (e.g., 200 concurrent sessions) over 15 minutes, hold for 30 minutes
   - Stress run: push 2x target concurrency to identify points of graceful degradation and fallback behavior
   - Configs: batching window 20ms, max batch size 128 (we will vary batching for sensitivity)
5) Success criteria / acceptance gates (proposal):
   - p95 latency for standard completion < 350ms for primary model at target concurrency
   - TTFT (first token) < 120ms on A100 for streaming requests
   - Sustained throughput >= 2,500 requests/sec (aggregate across a 3-instance pool) or tokens/sec equivalent
   - Error rate < 0.5% during sustained run
   - Regression tolerance: any change vs baseline > 10% in p95 or > 15% in TTFT requires root-cause and re-test
6) Data & security:
   - Use redacted traces or synthetic inputs; no PII to be uploaded to Redwood test clusters.
   - We can run on your VPC/private deployment if required (we'll need a 48h window to onboard infra).

Deliverables: workload spec (xlsx), raw metrics CSVs, latency/throughput dashboards, executive summary.

I'll prepare the workload spreadsheet and an initial Jenkins-like job config to run the tests. Please share the production trace sample link if you can.

— Diego
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
diego.fernandez@redwood.inference

Quick product-level framing to make sure acceptance criteria map to your business outcomes:

Key questions to validate during the benchmark:
- Does the primary model variant meet latency SLOs under expected concurrency? (this impacts UX for your checkout/chat flows)
- Does cost-per-1M-tokens stay within your budget threshold? We should include a cost proxy in the final report.
- Are there quality regressions when using quantized variants or when applying aggressive batching? We will run a small eval set to verify output quality doesn't regress beyond 1.5% of baseline on your scoring metric.

Suggested acceptance gates (mirrors Diego with one addition):
- Perf gate: p95 < 350ms at target concurrency (pass/fail)
- TTFT gate: p50 TTFT < 80ms, p95 TTFT < 120ms for streaming flows
- Quality gate: automated eval on 200 golden prompts; BLEU/ROUGE-like or custom metric within 1.5% of baseline
- Cost gate: projected monthly inference cost estimate using observed tokens/sec and the proposed Dedicated capacity configuration

If all gates pass after the week-4 run, we'll mark the technical MAP milestone satisfied and prepare the SOW/procurement ask.

I'll join the kickoff and will bring the small eval harness. Diego — thanks for the clear test matrix; I suggest we lock the exact eval prompts before the baseline run.

— Marissa
Product Manager, Benchmarks | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.inference

Thanks team — this looks reasonable and aligns with what we need to validate. A few replies inline and an initial ask: we can share a redacted 72-hour trace (link below).

On the workload: the request mix Diego suggests looks close. One note: our median prompt size is slightly higher because of product metadata (~120 tokens median). p95 around ~600. Streaming % is closer to 55% for the conversational path.

On SLOs and timeline: procurement wants a decision window by 2026-05-15. We have internal infra folks available to onboard a VPC test by next week but may prefer Redwood-hosted runs initially. Proposed MAP timeline (we need to meet procurement):
- 2026-04-20: Kickoff & finalize workload spec
- 2026-04-27: Baseline run completed (run 1) + interim results
- 2026-05-04: Tuning and run 2 (final)
- 2026-05-11: Executive review + decision prep
- 2026-05-15: Procurement decision date

We agree to the acceptance gates Marissa outlined; small tweak on p95 latency target to 400ms at p95 for the initial run on cost-optimized variant. If A100 shows the <350ms we will mark it a technical fit.
